# nish/net/quic-stream

The streams of one QUIC version 1 connection (RFC 9000 §2-§4): stream IDs and their four types, the sending and receiving state machines, reassembly, flow control per stream and for the connection, and the stream limits. Sans-IO, like the rest of `nish/net`: `nish/net/quic`'s `QuicConnection` hands it every stream frame it reads, asks it for the frames to send, and reports which of them a packet that was acknowledged or lost carried. An application reaches it through the connection's stream calls (`openStream`, `streamWrite`, `streamRead`, `nextStreamEvent` and the rest), not directly.

<scalar-callout type="info">

**IDs** (§2.1). The low bit says who opened a stream (0 the client, 1 the
server) and the next one whether it carries data both ways (0) or only
from its opener (1). This side is a server: it opens IDs 1 and 3 modulo 4,
and the client 0 and 2. A frame for a stream of the client's that is past
the limit this side advertised is STREAM_LIMIT_ERROR; for one of the
server's that it has not opened, STREAM_STATE_ERROR; and a frame that only
makes sense on a side the stream does not have (STREAM, RESET_STREAM or
STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED on the server's unidirectional stream; MAX_STREAM_DATA
or STOP_SENDING on the client's) is STREAM_STATE_ERROR (§19.4-§19.13). A
client's stream opens every lower one of its type with it (§3.2).

</scalar-callout>

<scalar-detail title="Fixed slots">

The table is sized once, from the configuration: one slot
per stream that may be open at once — as many client-opened bidirectional
and unidirectional streams as this side lets the client have, and
`localStreams` of its own. A stream lives in its slot from the frame (or
`open`) that starts it until both of its sides are done, and then the slot
is free for the next. A stream is found by its ID through a hash index,
never by a scan.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="Lent buffers">

A slot holds no buffers of its own. A side borrows a
`bufferSize`-byte buffer, and a bit per byte beside it, from the table's
`QuicStreamPools` when it first needs one: the receive side on the first
byte that lands, the send side on the first byte written. Each goes back,
its used extent zeroed, once it is done with: the receive side once the
application has read to the final size or the stream is reset, the send
side once every byte up to the final size is acknowledged or the stream
is reset, never before, since a lost byte is resent from the send buffer.
The pools hold two buffers per slot at most, the reserve's included, so a
borrow never fails, and
a server shares one pool across all its connections (`share`), so what it
holds follows the streams moving bytes, not the slots it was sized for.
Once the pools are warm, nothing a peer sends and nothing the application
writes allocates.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="Receiving">

**Receiving** (§3.2, §2.2). Data lands in the receive buffer at its offset
modulo the buffer's size, in any order and overlapping, with a bit set per
byte; what continues the stream from the last byte read is what
`read` hands out. The credit this side gives a stream (MAX_STREAM_DATA) is
never more than what the buffer can hold past the last byte read, so a
byte beyond it is FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR and the buffer cannot overflow; it is
raised by a whole buffer once the application has read half of one. The
connection's credit (MAX_DATA) is raised the same way, by `windowData`
once half of it is read. A FIN or RESET_STREAM fixes the final size, and
a frame that disagrees with it, or a size below what already arrived, is
FINAL_SIZE_ERROR (§4.5). A reset stream's bytes count as read for the
connection's credit.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="Sending">

**Sending** (§3.1). The application writes into the send buffer as far as
it has room, a chunk at a time: what `write` takes is its back-pressure,
and the stream's event fires again once acknowledgements free room. Bytes
stay in the buffer until acknowledged: the acknowledged bits move the
buffer's start, and a range a lost packet carried is sent again from it.
New bytes go out only within both the stream's credit and the
connection's; at either limit the stream owes STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED or the
connection DATA_BLOCKED, once per limit. A STOP_SENDING from the peer is
answered with RESET_STREAM (§3.5), and RESET_STREAM from the application
gives up what was not sent; either is sent until acknowledged.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-callout type="warning">

**Limits** (§4.6). The client may open as many streams of each type as
the configuration allows at once; MAX_STREAMS raises its limit as its
streams finish, once half of the configured number have. The server opens
streams within the client's limits and its own `localStreams`; past the
client's limit it owes STREAMS_BLOCKED.

</scalar-callout>

Written from RFC 9000 §2-§4 and §19, in this module's own structure;
nothing here is ported from another implementation. Private names carry
the `quicStream` prefix (`docs/wp26-stdlib.md` §3e).

## QuicStream

One stream slot. `id` is -1 while the slot is free. The fields are
readable — the states, `resetCode` once the peer reset it, `stopCode` once
it asked this side to stop — and written only by `QuicStreams`.

```ts
class QuicStream
```

| --- | --- |

| `blockedOwed: boolean` |  |
| `finAcked: boolean` |  |

## QuicStreamPools

The buffers a connection's streams borrow: `data` lends the receive and
send buffers of `bufferSize` bytes, `bits` the bitmaps beside them, a bit
per byte. One table makes a private set for itself; a server makes one set
for every slot and hands it to each connection's table with
`QuicStreams.share`, so the memory follows the streams moving bytes rather
than the slots the server was sized for. Each pool's ceiling is two
buffers for every stream it serves, one a side, which is what holding
every buffer at once costs. The reserve below counts against it too, so a
send side that finds the pools out takes the reserve's last buffer
(`lendSend`): with that side holding none, not every buffer is lent, and
the one left over is in the reserve.

Frames are handled inside the arena scope a packet is opened in, where
nothing may allocate, grow a list or push onto one. So the frames lend and
take back receive buffers through a reserve the pools keep beside their
free lists, by index alone: `lend` hands one out, `keep` takes one back
zeroed. Before each scope `prime` trims the reserve to `hold` buffers,
giving the rest to the pools, and tops it up to as many as the packet
could start receive sides, taking them. `hold` is one connection's stream
count, and the reserve three times that long, so a packet that lends
nothing and takes back every buffer its connection held still fits. Once
warm, the reserve mostly circulates on its own and `prime` costs a handful
of comparisons, with no take or give. The pools count the reserve's
buffers as lent. `prime` and the `drain` before each give-back outside a
packet trim it to `hold` for the whole server, not each connection, but
`keep` inside a packet can raise it to three times `hold`, and it stays
there until the next `prime` or `drain`.

```ts
class QuicStreamPools
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new QuicStreamPools(bufferSize: i32, streams: i32, connections: i32)` | Pools for `connections` connections of `streams` stream slots each, `bufferSize` bytes each way. |
| `bits: BufferPool` |  |
| `data: BufferPool` |  |
| `hold: i32` | The most the reserve keeps from one packet to the next: one connection's stream count. |
| `none: u8[]` | The empty array a free reserve entry holds. |
| `ready: i32` | How many buffers the reserve holds. |
| `readyBits: u8[][]` |  |
| `readyData: u8[][]` | The reserve: `ready` buffers and their bitmaps, taken from the pools and not lent to a stream; the rest of each list is `none`. |
| `room: i32` | How many buffers each pool's free list has been grown to hold, by `fit`. |
| `drain(most: i32): void` | Gives the reserve's buffers past the first `most` back to the pools, each already zeroed by `keep`. Never inside an arena scope. |
| `fit(): void` | Grows each pool's free list until it can hold every buffer the pool has made, by pushing `none` and popping it straight off again, so that a give-back never grows it. A slot's `reset` gives back every buffer its connection held at once, more than the free list ever held before, and the arena must not move by it (QUIC-3). The room doubles, so the pushes cost O(1) for each buffer made. |
| `keep(buf: u8[], have: u8[], used: i32): void` | Takes `buf` and its bitmap `have` back into the reserve, zeroing the first `used` bytes of the buffer and the bits of them. Safe inside an arena scope. Panics when the reserve is full: more given back between two `drain`s than one connection holds, a table's bug. |
| `lend(stream: QuicStream): void` | Lends the reserve's last buffer, into `stream`'s receive side. Panics when the reserve is empty: a packet handled without `prime`. |
| `lendSend(stream: QuicStream): void` | Lends `stream` a send buffer and bitmap: taken from the pools while they have one to give, else the reserve's last. The reserve counts against the same ceiling, so once the pools have made every buffer and lent them all, a send side wanting one means the reserve holds it. Never inside an arena scope, where a take would allocate. |
| `lent(): i32` | How many buffers and bitmaps are lent to streams now, the reserve's left out: 0 once every stream that borrowed has given back. |
| `prime(need: i32): void` | Readies the reserve for a packet that could start `need` receive sides: trims it to `hold` buffers, then tops it up to `need`. Takes and gives only when it is outside that window. Never inside an arena scope. |

## QuicStreams

The streams of one connection: their slots, the index by ID, the limits
both ways, the connection's flow control both ways, and the ring of
streams with something new for the application (`nextEvent`). The
counters are readable for a test or a log.

| `giveSend(stream: QuicStream): void` | Gives `stream`'s send buffer and bitmap back to the pools, zeroing every byte a write reached: below `sendEnd`, which past a whole buffer is all of it. Called only once nothing can be sent again from it — every byte acknowledged, or the side reset — and before a reset moves `sendEnd` back. |
| `indexInsert(k: i32, id: i64): void` | Puts slot `k` in the index under its stream's ID. |
| `indexRemove(k: i32, id: i64): void` | Takes slot `k`, holding `id`, out of the index, moving later entries of its probe run back so none is lost. |
| `locate(id: i64, receiving: boolean): i32` | The slot a frame for stream `id` refers to (§3.2, §4.6, §19.8): opening it, and every lower stream of its type, when it is the peer's and new. `receiving` says whether the frame is about the stream's receiving half (STREAM, RESET_STREAM, STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED) or its sending half (STOP_SENDING, MAX_STREAM_DATA). Answers the slot; -1 for a stream that finished and is gone, whose frames are ignored; or -2 with `locateError` holding STREAM_LIMIT_ERROR for the peer's stream past the limit, or STREAM_STATE_ERROR for one of this side's that it has not opened or a unidirectional stream without the half the frame is about (§19.4-§19.13). |
| `nextEvent(): i64` | The ID of the next stream with something new for the application — a stream the peer opened, bytes or a FIN to read, a reset, a STOP_SENDING, or room to write again after a short write — or -1 when there is none. Each stream comes up once however much happened to it; read and write it until it has nothing more to say. |
| `noteChunk(id: i64, offset: i64, length: i32, fin: boolean): void` | Describes the STREAM frame just written, for the packet's record. |
| `onMaxData(limit: i64): void` | MAX_DATA (§19.9): more credit for the connection. |
| `onMaxStreamData(id: i64, limit: i64): i64` | MAX_STREAM_DATA (§19.10): more credit for the stream. Answers 0 or the transport error. |
| `onMaxStreams(uni: boolean, limit: i64): void` | MAX_STREAMS (§19.11): the peer lets this side open more streams of a type. |
| `onReset(id: i64, code: i64, finalSize: i64): i64` | RESET_STREAM (§19.4): the peer abandons the stream at `finalSize` with `code`. Answers 0 or the transport error. |
| `onStopSending(id: i64, code: i64): i64` | STOP_SENDING (§19.5): the peer wants no more of the stream, which this side answers with RESET_STREAM carrying the same code (§3.5). Answers 0 or the transport error. |
| `onStream(id: i64, offset: i64, buf: u8[], from: i32, length: i32, fin: boolean): i64` | A STREAM frame: `length` bytes of `buf` from `from`, at stream offset `offset`, and the FIN when `fin`. Answers 0, or the transport error that closes the connection: the stream's ID (see `locate`), a stream only this side sends on, the final size, or the credit. |
| `onStreamDataBlocked(id: i64): i64` | STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED (§19.13): only the ID is checked; credit follows reading, not asking. |
| `open(bidi: boolean): i64` | Opens a stream of this side's (§2.1): bidirectional when `bidi`, else unidirectional. Answers its ID, or `QUIC_STREAM_ERR_LIMIT` when the peer's limit is reached (STREAMS_BLOCKED is then owed) or every slot for this side's streams is taken. |
| `openSlot(id: i64): i32` | Opens `id` in a free slot with its first credits; answers the slot, or -1 when none is free. |
| `ownPools(): QuicStreamPools \| null` | The pools, made for this table alone on first use when nothing shared one: a table that never moves a byte makes none. `null` when the streams have no buffers at all. Pools of one connection make every buffer the table could hold at once, there and then, the footprint the table had when each slot owned its buffers: how many it holds turns on when the peer acknowledges, so a lazily grown private pool would go on allocating after any warm-up. A server's shared pools grow lazily. |
| `prime(bytes: i32): void` | Readies the pools for a packet of `bytes` bytes, before the arena scope its frames are handled in: one buffer for every receive side it could start, which is no more than the sides holding none, nor than one per three bytes (the smallest STREAM frame carrying a byte, but for a last one without a length).<br><br>The peer's remaining stream credit is no tighter bound: an ACK earlier in the same packet can finish a stream, and `release` then raises the limit before a later STREAM frame opens past the old one. A bound that allows for every such release is one buffer per side holding none, which `idle` already is. Once warm the buffers a packet gives back refill the reserve for the next one, so this costs a handful of comparisons, not a take per side. |
| `pushFree(k: i32): void` | Puts slot `k` on the free stack. |
| `putNew(stream: QuicStream, k: i32, buf: u8[], at: i32, end: i32): i32` | One STREAM frame of `stream`'s new bytes within both credits. A stream held back by a credit owes the matching BLOCKED frame, once per limit. |
| `putNextChunk(buf: u8[], at: i32, end: i32): i32` | Writes one STREAM frame into `buf[at .. end)` for the next stream, in turn, that has one to send: its lost bytes first, else as many new ones as fit and both credits allow, with the FIN when the rest fits. Answers the offset past it, with `lastId`, `lastOffset`, `lastLength` and `lastFin` describing it for the packet's record; or `at` when no stream has a frame that fits. |
| `putNextControl(buf: u8[], at: i32, end: i32): i32` | Writes the next control frame owed, if it fits in `buf[at .. end)`: MAX_DATA, the MAX_STREAMS and BLOCKED frames, then each stream's MAX_STREAM_DATA, STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED, RESET_STREAM and STOP_SENDING. Answers the offset past it, with `lastKind` (a `QUIC_STREAM_CONTROL_*`) and `lastValue` (the stream it names, or 0) for the packet's record; or `at` when nothing owed fits. |
| `putResend(stream: QuicStream, buf: u8[], at: i32, end: i32): i32` | One STREAM frame of what `stream` lost: its lost bytes, skipping those acknowledged since, with the FIN only when they run to the final size (§4.5); or, with no bytes left to send again, a lost FIN alone, as a frame of no bytes at the final size. |
| `putStreamControl(stream: QuicStream, buf: u8[], at: i32, end: i32): i32` | The next control frame `stream` owes, if it fits; sets `lastKind`. |
| `queue(k: i32): void` | Puts slot `k` on the event ring, unless it is there already. |
| `read(id: i64, buf: u8[], at: i32, length: i32): i32` | Reads up to `length` bytes of stream `id` into `buf` from `at`. Answers how many it read; 0 when nothing is there yet; `QUIC_STREAM_END` once every byte up to the FIN was read; `QUIC_STREAM_ERR_RESET` once the peer reset it; or another `QUIC_STREAM_ERR_*`. Reading half a buffer gives the peer more credit. A stream's receiving side is done when a read answers `QUIC_STREAM_END` or `QUIC_STREAM_ERR_RESET`, so read until one does. After `QuicConnection.release`, a stream that still owed bytes answers `QUIC_STREAM_END` and copies nothing: its buffer went back to the pool. |
| `release(k: i32): void` | Frees slot `k` once both of its stream's sides are done (§3.3). A stream the peer opened counts toward raising its limit: MAX_STREAMS is owed once half the configured number have finished since the last one. |
| `reset(): void` | Frees every slot and puts every counter back, for a connection slot reused for another peer. Every buffer a stream still held goes back to its pool first. |
| `resetSlot(k: i32, code: i64): void` | Abandons the sending side of slot `k` with `code` (§3.1, §19.4): what was not sent is dropped and RESET_STREAM is owed. |
| `resetStream(id: i64, code: i64): i32` | Resets stream `id`'s sending side with `code`. Answers `QUIC_STREAM_OK` or a `QUIC_STREAM_ERR_*`. |
| `setPeerLimits(maxData: i64, bidiLocal: i64, bidiRemote: i64, uni: i64, maxStreamsBidi: i64, maxStreamsUni: i64): void` | Takes the peer's transport parameters (RFC 9000 §18.2): its limits on the streams this side opens, the credit each kind of stream starts with, and the connection's. |
| `share(pools: QuicStreamPools): void` | Borrows the stream buffers from `pools` from now on, in place of the table's own: how a server's connections share one set. Call it before any stream has borrowed, or after `reset`. Panics when the pools' buffers are not `bufferSize` bytes. |
| `slotOf(id: i64): i32` | The slot of stream `id`, or -1 when it is not open. |
| `stopSending(id: i64, code: i64): i32` | Asks the peer to stop sending on stream `id`, with `code` (STOP_SENDING, §3.5). Answers `QUIC_STREAM_OK` or a `QUIC_STREAM_ERR_*`. |
| `streamControlLost(kind: i32, id: i64): void` | A lost control frame of stream `id`. |
| `takeFree(): i32` | Takes a free slot off the stack, or -1 when every slot is in use. |
| `write(id: i64, buf: u8[], from: i32, length: i32, fin: boolean): i32` | Writes up to `length` bytes of `buf` from `from` to stream `id`, and its FIN when `fin` and every byte fit. Answers how many bytes it took — fewer than `length` when the send buffer is full, and the stream's event fires once acknowledgements free room — or a `QUIC_STREAM_ERR_*`. |

## Limits

<scalar-grid cols="2">

<scalar-card title="3" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_STREAM_CONTROL_MAX_DATA: i32`

MAX_DATA, the connection's credit.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="5" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_STREAM_CONTROL_MAX_STREAMS_BIDI: i32`

MAX_STREAMS for bidirectional streams.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="6" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_STREAM_CONTROL_MAX_STREAMS_UNI: i32`

MAX_STREAMS for unidirectional streams.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="4" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_STREAM_CONTROL_MAX_STREAM_DATA: i32`

MAX_STREAM_DATA for the stream the record's value names.

</scalar-card>

</scalar-grid>

## Constants

<scalar-grid cols="2">

<scalar-card title="3" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_RECV_DATA_READ: i32`

Every byte was read: the side is done (§3.2 "Data Read").

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="2" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_RECV_DATA_RECVD: i32`

Every byte up to the final size arrived (§3.2 "Data Recvd").

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="6" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_RECV_NONE: i32`

The stream has no receiving side here: a unidirectional stream this side opened.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_RECV_RECV: i32`

Receiving, the final size not known yet (§3.2 "Recv").

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="5" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_RECV_RESET_READ: i32`

The application saw the reset: the side is done (§3.2 "Reset Read").

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="4" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_RECV_RESET_RECVD: i32`

The peer reset the stream (§3.2 "Reset Recvd").

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="1" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_RECV_SIZE_KNOWN: i32`

The FIN fixed the final size; bytes are still missing (§3.2 "Size Known").

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="3" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_SEND_DATA_RECVD: i32`

Every byte and the FIN acknowledged: the side is done (§3.1 "Data Recvd").

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="2" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_SEND_DATA_SENT: i32`

Every byte and the FIN sent, not all acknowledged (§3.1 "Data Sent").

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="6" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_SEND_NONE: i32`

The stream has no sending side here: a unidirectional stream the peer opened.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_SEND_READY: i32`

A sending side with nothing written yet (§3.1 "Ready").

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="5" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_SEND_RESET_RECVD: i32`

RESET_STREAM acknowledged: the side is done (§3.1 "Reset Recvd").

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="4" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_SEND_RESET_SENT: i32`

RESET_STREAM sent, not yet acknowledged (§3.1 "Reset Sent").

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="1" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_SEND_SEND: i32`

Data written, not all of it sent with the FIN (§3.1 "Send").

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="7" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_STREAM_CONTROL_DATA_BLOCKED: i32`

DATA_BLOCKED.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="11" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_STREAM_CONTROL_RESET: i32`

RESET_STREAM for the stream the value names.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="12" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_STREAM_CONTROL_STOP_SENDING: i32`

STOP_SENDING for the stream the value names.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="9" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_STREAM_CONTROL_STREAMS_BLOCKED_BIDI: i32`

STREAMS_BLOCKED for bidirectional streams.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="10" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_STREAM_CONTROL_STREAMS_BLOCKED_UNI: i32`

STREAMS_BLOCKED for unidirectional streams.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="8" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_STREAM_CONTROL_STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED: i32`

STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED for the stream the value names.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-7" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_STREAM_END: i32`

A read past the end: every byte up to the FIN has been read.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-5" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_STREAM_ERR_DIRECTION: i32`

The stream has no such side: a write to a stream only the peer sends on, or a read of one only this side sends on.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-2" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_STREAM_ERR_FINISHED: i32`

The stream's sending side is finished: a FIN was written, or the stream was reset.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-3" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_STREAM_ERR_FLOW: i32`

The data would pass the credit the peer gave, or the room in the send buffer (all-or-nothing `writeStream`).

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-6" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_STREAM_ERR_LIMIT: i32`

No stream can be opened now: the peer's MAX_STREAMS is reached (STREAMS_BLOCKED is sent), or every local slot is taken.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-8" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_STREAM_ERR_RESET: i32`

The peer reset the stream (RESET_STREAM): `resetCode` holds its error code.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-4" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_STREAM_ERR_STATE: i32`

The connection is not connected.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-9" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_STREAM_ERR_STOPPED: i32`

The peer asked this side to stop sending (STOP_SENDING), which reset the stream: `stopCode` holds its code.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-1" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_STREAM_ERR_UNKNOWN: i32`

No such stream: never opened, or already finished both ways and gone.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`QUIC_STREAM_OK: i32`

Done: the data was taken, or the frame queued.

</scalar-card>

</scalar-grid>
